newsitem.title: USA: NHL-LALIME, THREE CALDER FINALISTS HEAD ALL-ROOKIE TEAM.
newsitem.headline: NHL-LALIME, THREE CALDER FINALISTS HEAD ALL-ROOKIE TEAM.

text.p: Pittsburgh Penguins goaltender Patrick Lalime, who went his first 16 games without a loss, was one of six players selected to the NHL All-Rookie Team, the National Hockey League announced Tuesday.

Also included on the squad in voting by members of the Professional Hockey Writers' Association were the three finalists for the Calder Trophy -- forwards Jarome Iginla of the Calgary Flames, Jim Campbell of the St Louis Blues and defenceman Bryan Berard of the New York Islanders.
Completing the NHL All-Rookie Team were defenceman Janne Niinimaa of the Philadelphia Flyers and forward Sergei Berezin of the Toronto Maple Leafs.

Lalime, called upon when both Pittsburgh goaltenders Tom Barrasso and Ken Wregget were injured, made a spectacular debut for the Penguins, going 14-0-2 in his first 16 decisions -- a modern day record.
Lalime's streak included three shutouts before he cooled off and finished the season with a record of 21-12-2 and a 2.94 goals against average in 39 games.

Iginla finished the 1996-97 regular season with the most points in the NHL by a rookie with 50 on 21 goals and 29 assists, appearing in all 82 games for Calgary. He led all rookies in powerplay goals with eight.

Campbell, who had a goal and an assist in his debut with the Blues, recorded 43 points on 23 goals and 20 assists -- fourth among NHL rookies -- in just 68 games for St Louis. He tied for first among rookies with six game-winning goals.
Berard played all 82 games for the Islanders, leading all first-year defencemen with 48 points (8 goals, 40 assists) and finishing second to Iginla among rookies in scoring.
Berezin led all rookies in goals with 25 and finished with 41 points in 73 games for Toronto.
Niinimaa, who played for Finland in the World Cup in September, is the only All-Rookie Team member competing in the Stanley Cup finals.
He had four goals and 40 assists, and playing the point on a powerplay with Eric Lindros and John LeClair, finished first among rookies with 23 powerplay assists.
The winner of the Calder Trophy, given annually to the NHL's rookie of the year, will be announced June 19 in Toronto.
